name: Nahash
overview: Nahash was a male king of the Ammonites, an ancient Semitic tribe. He is uniquely identified as the King of the Ammonites in 1 Samuel 11:2. Nahash's role as a foreign monarch places him within the biblical narrative as a significant external figure interacting with Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Nahash means 'viper' or 'copper' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name with possible symbolic implications. He also held the title 'King of the sons of Ammon,' which straightforwardly identifies his royal authority over the Ammonite people as noted in 1 Samuel 12:12.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Nahash as a descendant of Ben-ammi, connecting him to the ancestral lineage of the Ammonites. He is also inferred to be the father of Hanun and Shobi, indicating a dynastic succession within the Ammonite monarchy.
scriptureSignificance: Nahash's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his position as the Ammonite king during a time of conflict with Israel. His leadership is noted in the context of interactions with the Israelite people, highlighting the ongoing tensions and political dynamics between Israel and surrounding nations. Nahash's role helps illustrate the challenges faced by Israel from neighboring kingdoms during the period of the judges and early monarchy.
